title: Kernel routing telemetry & attention-path probe playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: introduce a low-overhead, queryable telemetry surface for kernel routing and attention execution paths that enables per-request attribution, lightweight NVTX envelopes, and an attention-path probe that surfaces kernel selection reasons. This ticket is the playbook to land instrumentation, dashboards, and rollout steps.
acceptance_criteria: Per-request exec_id mapping is emitted for >=95% of sampled requests with <1% added p99 latency overhead.
NVTX envelope naming convention documented and produced by runtime for prefill and decode stages (prefix: redwood.exec.<stage>.<kernel_family>.<reason>).
New metrics published to statsd/Prometheus: kernel_active_ms, kernel_queue_ms, kernel_choice_reason (tagged), attention_path_variant, per_kernel_mac_count (sampled).
Example traces in Zipkin/Jaeger show joined spans from API->scheduler->kernel and display kernel_choice_reason in the UI.
Dashboard tile (Console) with top-10 kernel choices by model and sequence length and a heatmap of attention_path_variant vs latency is available.
Instrumentation gated behind runtime config flag runtime.telemetry.kernel_probe and rolloutable via feature flag.
Security review completed and telemetry contains no customer prompt payloads or raw tokens (only hashed identifiers where necessary).
tasks: Design envelope & tag schema for NVTX ranges and span names (authored in this ticket).
Implement exec_id propagation through scheduler -> worker -> kernel launcher (C++ runtime).
Add lightweight kernel_choice_reason enum and attach as span tag and metric label.
Implement attention-path probe: collect a compact fingerprint of attention pathway (dense/flash/kv-merged) per sampled request.
Wire metrics to Prometheus/statsd and add translation for Console ingestion pipeline.
Create Console dashboard and example queries (PromQL/SQL).
Add e2e tests and perf guardrails in CI to ensure overhead <1% p99 latency.
Draft rollout plan and enablement doc for SRE/Support.
notes: Design decisions: prefer sampled, envelope-style NVTX ranges to continuous high-cardinality spans. We will encode metadata in envelope headers and attach concise tags to spans instead of serializing full context objects.
Trade-offs: per-kernel counters at full sample rate are high-cardinality; we will sample 1 in 100 requests by default and allow project-level overrides. Use reservoir sampling for long-lived streams.
Metric naming: use dot-delimited namespace kernel.<family>.<metric> for Prometheus-friendly labels; kernel.choice_reason will be a label enumerated to known values to avoid label explosion.
Privacy: do not emit prompt text or raw tokens. Exec_id will be a stable hashed identifier (sha1) salted by customer id for debug but not reversible.
Fallback behavior: if trace exporter is unavailable, runtime should still emit counters and buffered spans to disk for later submission.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary) — enable kernel_probe on dedicated canary capacity for 48 hours, sampling at 0.01x.
Phase 2 (Scale) — increase sampling to 0.1x and enable dashboards; run for 7 days and validate signal quality.
Phase 3 (Ramp) — default sampling 1x on debug/flaky mode only; expose feature flag to customers and internal tenants.
Rollback — ability to disable runtime.telemetry.kernel_probe and flush buffered metrics.
test_plan: Unit tests for exec_id propagation and enum serialization.
Integration test that produces a trace with prefill and decode spans and verifies kernel_choice_reason tag appears.
Perf benchmark harness that compares baseline latency vs instrumented runtime with 10k synthetic requests.
Manual QA: run against small model fleet and validate Console dashboard values match local profiler.
